transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-11-09 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Priya Nair (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lina Cho (Redwood CSM); Elaine Park (Verdant SRE), Jonas Meyer (Verdant VP Eng), Samir Khan (Verdant Security), Rita Gomez (Verdant Platform)

Summary (auto): short recap of the 11/02 outage, proposed mitigations, scheduling for pilot on dedicated capacity and security artifact handoff.

[00:00] Priya Nair: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. We wanted to run through the postmortem follow-up, make sure we have concrete owners for the fixes and the pilot plan. Marco's gonna lead the tech bits.
[00:12] Marco Ruiz: yep, hi all. Quick apology again from the infra team. We dug in - root cause was a combination of a memory leak in our runtime's attention cache handling when certain long-context requests arrived, plus the autoscaler cooldown/profile that delayed adding capacity. The leak cause - it's not a model bug, it's in the serving path, in the kv cache handling for long prefixes. Transcription: "K V cash" in some logs which is weird but you know how speech to text does that.
[00:37] Elaine Park: just to be clear, that translated to GPU OOMs and timeouts across about 3% of your serving pods right? We saw spikes starting ~14:02 UTC on 11/02 and then cascading.
[00:46] Marco Ruiz: yeah exactly. A few pods hit OOM; our fallback policy retried to other pods which increased latency and then the autoscaler didn't spin up new machines quickly enough because the cooldown for our spillover policy was set conservatively. Also we had a small bug in our rolling restart logic that briefly double-scheduled migrations.
[01:10] Jonas Meyer: you mentioned fallback retries - why did requests keep retrying instead of circuit breaking earlier? That was our biggest production pain, customers got error pages.
[01:19] Marco Ruiz: good callout. Our circuit breaker threshold was tuned for general latency, not for this rare mem leak pattern; when errors were transient it retried, causing amplification. We're proposing an immediate change to the circuit breaker to fail-fast for OOM signatures.
[01:34] Samir Khan: security question - any chance logs leaked customer data during that window? We need to know retention and whether any PII was in the core dumps.
[01:44] Priya Nair: excellent question. We reviewed the crash dumps - so far no PII found; crash logs are sanitized before export. We'll include the raw sanitized traces in the packet we send. Also note that our KMS keys rotated as expected; no KMS compromise. But we will include KMS rotation logs.
[02:05] Elaine Park: we also want an SLA for these kinds of degradation modes. Can we get a runbook?
[02:12] Lina Cho: yes, CS will provide a runbook and an on-call escalation for Verdant. We'll also add a postmortem doc with RCA and mitigations - I'll send that today.
[02:25] Marco Ruiz: technical mitigations: 1) hotfix to kill the leaking allocation path in the kv cache and add guardrails. 2) reduce autoscaler cooldown and add an emergency fast-path that can spin up burst capacity for OOM-driven failures. 3) adjust circuit breaker to detect OOM/errors and trip faster. 4) add extra telemetry (per-pod memory growth alarms) and a dashboard.
[02:49] Jonas Meyer: what's the ETA for the hotfix to be validated? Can we get a canary run on a dedicated pool? Our legal team only wants dedicated or VPC for expanded scope.
[02:59] Marco Ruiz: we have a patch ready in a branch, but need to validate. Proposal: run canary on a 4-node dedicated pool with your test workload next week. We can target 11/16 for a bench + canary.
[03:12] Rita Gomez: we need to confirm networking - will the dedicated pool be in our V P C? We can't route cross-tenant traffic.
[03:19] Priya Nair: yes, the Dedicated offering supports customer VPC peering and private subnets. We'll prepare a network runbook. There was one doc link we shared earlier - I'll re-share it.
[03:30] Elaine Park: also curious about backups/rollbacks - if we push the hotfix and something else regresses, what's rollback time and plan?
[03:39] Marco Ruiz: rollback is immediate if canary fails; the serving control plane supports instant traffic cutover to a matching model variant on older runtime. We'll also keep the old pool warm for 24 hours.
[03:50] Samir Khan: for compliance we need the SOC2 binder and any HIPAA notes. You mentioned earlier you could share that?
[03:57] Priya Nair: yes, I'll share the SOC2 binder and the HIPAA-specific gap notes. We'll include KMS integration notes, audit-log retention policy, and SAML/SSO configs. Expect those docs in the postmortem packet.
[04:12] Marco Ruiz: additional long-term suggestions: profiled GC for GPU memory, improved KV cache eviction heuristics by prefix length, and a scheduler tweak to avoid double migrations under high churn. We'll file these as backlog items.
[04:29] Jonas Meyer: about cost - if we move to Dedicated for the pilot, what's the estimated incremental cost for a week of benchmarking? We need a ballpark to run past procurement.
[04:38] Priya Nair: rough estimate: for a 4-node A100-equivalent pool for one week, engineering benchmarks + canary, ballpark $6k-$9k depending on run time and storage. We'll send an itemized estimate in the follow-up email.
[04:53] Elaine Park: can you also include the per-token cost delta when using the dedicated pool versus hosted? We need that for capacity planning.
[04:59] Priya Nair: yes - we'll include a cost delta table and recommend quant/ batching profiles that reduce unit costs.
[05:10] [Speaker 2 - likely Marco]: small note, we saw two unrelated slow API calls due to a third-party network flap; we scrubbed that from the RCA but it's in the timeline.
[05:23] Lina Cho: ok next steps recap: Redwood to send timeline + logs, Marco to prepare hotfix and canary plan, schedule pilot for 11/16, CS to send runbook and SOC2/HIPAA docs. Samir to confirm any extra compliance items.
[05:35] Jonas Meyer: do we have a postmortem doc link now or will you send after this call?
[05:41] Priya Nair: I'll send the doc after the call; Lina will finalize the RCA section and then we'll get it to you.
[05:48] Elaine Park: thanks, appreciate the transparency. One ask: can we have a 1-hour follow-up after the canary to review telemetry and decide on rollout?
[05:55] Marco Ruiz: absolutely. We'll book a slot for 11/17.
[06:00] Priya Nair: ok thanks everyone. We'll email the packet and next steps.
[06:06] [end]
